answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a licensed alpine yarrow plot irrigated by glacier meltwater. A botanical registrar weighs each harvest in person and presses it into an umber-stamped herbarium sheet keyed to that identity; random spot-checks summon the holder to their own plot within a day, and one grower cannot tend two plots at once. The plot fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real plot, another season of alpine labor, another human, and twice the prior fee.
